quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should your following distance be?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between your car and a motorcycle. You need this extra space in case the motorcycle and rider fall into the road.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Have done as much as you can.
Must stay until the police arrive.
Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner of the parked car. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in your current direction.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the others?
questions.explanation: Follow directions from traffic officers before signs, signals, or road markings. Traffic officers include police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They do not need more space to turn than cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars because they are larger and heavier.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other cars?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, there is more risk of a collision. If you drive faster than traffic around you, you will keep having to pass. Drive with traffic flow within the speed limit and only pass when you need to.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. On a road with multiple lanes, move into the left lane before you reach the turn. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then turn when the road is clear.

questions.question: When turning left, which traffic light gives you the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you when turning.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when leaving an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bike, and if someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. You can reduce the risk by driving more slowly.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look drunk. Opening a window, playing the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Drinking coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. Shaded spots are the last to dry. Be extra careful on roads shaded by trees or buildings.

questions.question: When a traffic signal light turns green, you should:

options.text: Not move until another driver waves you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, let any traffic and pedestrians still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road where traffic backs up behind you, pull off the road to let other vehicles pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit when you must.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn then.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn then.
questions.explanation: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Let any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection go first. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Do not brake hard. Slowly release the accelerator and gently apply the brakes once you are moving slowly. Then pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane with you.
Pass the motorcycle using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give a motorcycle driver a full lane. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights or a siren, you must yield. Move as far to the right side of the road as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When you see a solid green arrow on a traffic signal, what can you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane pointed to by the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow tells you that you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up right away.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn of construction or maintenance on the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: Which action is not allowed for a passenger in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink from or have an open alcohol container in a moving vehicle on a public road. Breaking this law has serious penalties for the driver.
